setup: Hips in line with the machine's pivot
Back pad just below your shoulder blades
Feet on the footrests, belt or pad on
execution: Brace and keep your spine long
Push back against the pad smoothly
Stop when your torso lines up with legs
Let it forward slowly, then repeat
faults: Don't throw yourself into the pad
Don't round over hard at the front

notes: Start light; the stack resists the whole time, including where the back is most bent.
Use a pain-free range. Stop each rep at upright rather than arching backward.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at seat height, seat back pad on the right of the figure, machine pivot level with the hips. Pad and lever arm drawn behind the upper back.

keyPositions.label: Forward
keyPositions.describe: Seated with hips at the pivot, feet on the footrests. Torso leaning forward from the hips, back long, pad resting just below the shoulder blades. Arms crossed or holding the handles.

keyPositions.label: Upright
keyPositions.describe: Torso pushed back to upright, in line with the thighs' upright seat line, pad pressed back. Spine long, not arched backward.

ikHints: Hips and feet fixed on the seat and footrests
Back pad stays in contact with the upper back
emphasise: Movement from the hips with a long spine

uncertain.note: "Back extension", "Hyperextension" and "Lower back extension(s)" are deliberately not aliases: the first two belong to the 45° back extension, and the third is ambiguous (batch-03). An import should ask Ben which machine he means.
Aligning the hips with the pivot comes from a search summary (Liftosaur and others), not from a fetched page.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data. Machine designs differ: some rotate the seat, some only the back pad.
